dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?

Hi, yes, hi. I'm calling about a storm drain, well, the water, it's not going down. On Harrison Avenue. It's my mother's street, I'm calling for her, she's in her seventies and she's not going to call herself. So.
Okay, sure. What's the address you're talking about?
352 Harrison Avenue, Fort Adams side. Down toward the end, you know, where it dips.
Got it. And what's it doing out there right now?

Right now it's lower than it was, but it's, the water's over the curb and across the whole sidewalk. It was like that yesterday too, and this is two days after the nor'easter, the one that ended Saturday. Two days. It's not even raining. Mom can't get out the front without walking through it. Hang on, Dominic, I said hang on, put it down. Sorry. Sorry.
No worries, take your time. Is the water in the road itself too, or just at the curb?

The road too. A delivery truck got stuck in it this morning, like, a big box truck, it tried to pull up by her neighbor's and it just sat there. The driver was out there, he was not happy. Somebody had to, I don't know, he finally backed out. And I thought, this is going to keep happening, so.
Yeah, that sounds like the drain's blocked up somewhere. Has anyone looked at it, or have you noticed what's on the grate?

I did. I went over Sunday and cleared the leaves off the grate by hand, a whole pile, wet, disgusting, and it helped. For about ten minutes. Then it just, it filled right back up. So it's not only leaves, there's something, it's down in there. And honestly this isn't the first time that corner has done this, it's always, nobody ever comes and, Dominic, no. No. I'm on the phone.

Okay. So you cleared the grate and it drained a little, then backed up again. That tells me it's probably clogged farther down the line. I'll put in a request for a crew to check that drain and the pipe. Do you have a number where they can reach you?
Yeah, it's 401-555-0167. That's the house phone here, I'm at my own place but I'm giving you mine, because Mom doesn't always hear it.
Okay, 401-555-0167, and your name?
Theresa Fiore. F-I-O-R-E.
Thank you, Theresa. And the address again, 352 Harrison Avenue?

Right, 352. Can I ask, who do I call if it's still like this tomorrow? Because I don't want to just wait and have it be Thursday and the whole street is a pond. Who's the person to call to get it checked, like, actually checked?

You can call this same line, Public Works, and ask for the status on the request. I'll note that the water's across the sidewalk and that a truck got stuck, so it gets flagged as a traffic and access issue. Crews are busy after a storm like that, so I can't give you an hour, but it'll go on the list today.

Okay. Today. Okay. Because it's, I mean, it's been two days. And if it freezes, she's going to be walking on ice. She's got that bad hip, she can't, Dominic! Sorry. Sorry, he's got, the cartoon ended and now he wants a snack.
I hear it. Take your time.

Thanks. And it's just a mess today, honestly, my whole schedule is off. They moved my show to Wednesday this week. My favorite one, it's always Monday, and now it's Wednesday, and I'm like, can anything just stay where it's supposed to be.
Oh, that's annoying. Mine does that around the holidays too. They shuffle everything.
Right? Anyway. Sorry. So you'll send somebody to look at the drain, not just put the note in.

The note is the request, and it goes to the crew supervisor. They'll send someone to inspect the drain. If it's something they can clear with the equipment on the truck, they'll do that. If it's a collapsed pipe or something bigger, that gets scheduled separately.
Okay. Well, I don't want to be, you know, I'm not trying to be difficult. It's just that it keeps happening and we keep waiting.

No, you're not being difficult. A drain that's still holding water two days later needs eyes on it. Meanwhile, if you can, tell your mom to stay off the curb side where it's deepest, and keep anyone from driving through it.
Yeah, I'll tell her. She's going to say she's fine. She's always fine. Okay. So I've got you down, Denise, was it?
Denise, yes. If you call back, mention 352 Harrison and the storm drain request from today, Monday, and whoever picks up can find it.
Okay. Thank you. I appreciate it. Dominic, what did I say about the, okay, bye, thanks, bye.
Bye now, Theresa.
